turns.input: I'm demo customer DEMO-1001. Playback 8.6.2 on my iPad says Cloud Pro expired. Can you check whether my demo subscription is active and whether a newer version has a documented fix?
turns.reply:
Let me compare your version against recent releases.

Your demo Cloud Pro subscription is active through March 14, 2027. Playback 8.6.3 documented a fix for this false expired message; do you have time to update now?

customer.name: Jordan Avery
customer.notes: Active Cloud Pro subscriber. Reports a 'Cloud Pro expired' message in Playback despite an active plan. Last known Playback version 8.6.2 (iPad).

matchingNotes: Subscriptions: fixed a false 'Cloud Pro expired' message that appeared for some active subscribers.
Rentals & MT Complete: fixed three issues involving custom arrangements, interrupted MT Complete previews, and 'Song Data Error' messages after using Restore From Cloud.
allNotes: Subscriptions: fixed a false 'Cloud Pro expired' message that appeared for some active subscribers.
Improvements: removed the 'New' badge from MT Complete in the Add Song menu; reworded the low memory alert.
Rentals & MT Complete: fixed three issues involving custom arrangements, interrupted MT Complete previews, and 'Song Data Error' messages after using Restore From Cloud.
Setlists: fixed the waveform and mixer not loading after adding the first song; fixed a search display issue in the Open Setlists menu.
Mac & Keyboard Shortcuts: fixed a Cmd+, conflict so it consistently opens Playback Settings.
Audio & MIDI: improved MIDI Out stability during playback.

gaps: App Store version is 8.6.4 but the release notes text refers to Playback 8.6.3. Treat the notes as possibly belonging to an earlier release.
App Store shows 8.6.4 but documented release notes only go up to 8.6.3; changes in between are not covered.
result.updateCaution: Updating closes Playback and takes a few minutes, so it should wait until after a service or rehearsal.
result.guidance: A documented fix exists in a newer version. Say which version fixed it, then give the caution in one sentence before suggesting the update; offer a non-disruptive step first if the caller is mid-service.
